logline: A fictional T20 franchise becomes the battleground for match-fixing cartels, ownership wars, and political patronage - the sport as a front for every kind of power.

renewal.note: The series concluded after three seasons in December 2021. No further seasons have been announced.

bollymeter.basis: The debut season of the first Hindi Amazon Original earned an International Emmy nomination for Best Drama and an IMDb 7.9, with Film Companion noting some of the smartest writing seen in an Indian show at the time.

pull_quotes.text: The writing is some of the smartest I have seen in an Indian show.

seasons.review_body: Inside Edge Season 1 launched on July 10, 2017, as Amazon Prime Video's first Hindi-language original - a milestone that lent it extra scrutiny. Created by Karan Anshuman and produced by Excel Entertainment, the ten-episode season follows the Mumbai Mavericks T20 franchise through a spot-fixing conspiracy that implicates owners, players, and politicians. India Today called it perfectly cast and technically first rate. Film Companion praised the intelligence of the writing while noting generic filmmaking. The season earned a nomination at the 46th International Emmy Awards for Best Drama Series, the clearest external validation Indian streaming had received to that point. IMDb settled the series at 7.9.

episode_reviews.title: Pilot
episode_reviews.review_body: Inside Edge Episode 1 aired July 10, 2017 on Amazon Prime Video as the opening chapter of India's first Hindi-language Amazon Original - a milestone that ensured it received close scrutiny. The premiere establishes the Mumbai Mavericks T20 franchise's ownership architecture with efficiency: Vivek Oberoi's team owner is drawn as morally compromised from the first scene, Richa Chadha's team manager as someone navigating a system she did not design and cannot fully control. The fixing syndicate's reach is introduced through a single exchange that functions as the season's premise crystallised - the scene the Film Companion review identified when calling the writing 'some of the smartest I have seen in an Indian show.' The International Emmy nomination for Best Drama Series that followed Season 1 confirmed that India's streaming ambition had arrived at a credible level of craft.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the Mumbai Mavericks' ownership structure, introduces the key players across the cricket-crime divide, and sets the show's tone as prestige pulp. Vivek Oberoi's team owner and Richa Chadha's team manager are both drawn with genuine complexity from the first episode.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The scene that reveals how deep the fixing syndicate reaches - the show's premise crystallised in a single exchange.

bollymeter.basis: Critics found Season 2 consistent with the debut; the show broadened its corruption canvas to national cricket while maintaining the ensemble quality.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived December 6, 2019, expanding the conspiracy from a single franchise to the machinery of Indian cricket at the national level. The season retained the ensemble from Season 1 and introduced new antagonists representing institutional corruption. The writing and direction maintained steady quality, keeping the show’s identity without significant deterioration. The Rotten Tomatoes sample stayed too small to support a reliable aggregate, while IMDb engagement held near even with the debut. Siddhant Chaturvedi's arc stands out as a highlight.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 widens the canvas from franchise corruption to the national board; the show's scale increases without a commensurate drop in coherence.

bollymeter.basis: A Subhash K Jha review on IMDb called Season 3 still edgy and engrossing; the series maintained its quality across the run without a sharp decline.

seasons.review_body: The third and final season launched December 3, 2021, bringing the Mumbai Mavericks saga to a close with international cricket as the new arena. Season 3 received less critical coverage than the debut but existing reviews remained favourable. Subhash K Jha on IMDb News described it as still edgy and engrossing, noting the show had not surrendered the tension of its earlier seasons. The audience maintained consistent loyalty across all three seasons; the IMDb aggregate for the series held steady at 7.9. The show's three-season run stands as one of the more coherent long-form arcs in Indian streaming.
seasons.season_over_season: The finale season moves to international cricket and brings the overarching corruption arc toward resolution; reviewer consensus held that quality did not materially drop in the third year.
